items.guidance: Inspect the s6-overlay service definitions referenced by the Dockerfile to separate the one-shot init services (init-complete, init-custom-init, init-env-file, init-folders and similar) from the long-running ones. Only the long-running ones become web or worker processes. If a bundled Redis or similar broker service appears among them, report it as provided by Deployz Valkey instead of declaring a worker.

Check whether the app's settings already support S3-compatible storage by configuration, and report those variable names if they exist. If they do, change no code. For /usr/src/paperless/data, separate persistent content from caches or indexes that can be regenerated, and treat any media or consume directories configured alongside it the same way.

psycopg indicates a Django backend despite the node runtime label, so check the image's init scripts for a migrate call at startup. If one exists, report that file. Also confirm that the database settings can read the Deployz-injected DATABASE_* variables.

Check the Python sources and s6 service definitions for the Celery app module and any celery beat scheduler, and report how each is started. Also report whether the broker URL setting can read the Deployz-injected REDIS_URL.
